messages:
Alex Chen: thinking about adding a compact "route reason" header to responses so downstream services can show why a request went to a fallback model. e.g. X-Redwood-Route-Reason: tier=fallback;cause=capacity;variant=quant4
Samir Rao: +1 for the idea. will help debugging in customer apps. question: do we expose full policy evaluation or just a short enum? :thinking:
Maria Lopez: prefer a short enum + trace_id that links to internal decision log. we should avoid leaking policy details to customers.
Kevin Patel: agree with Maria. also need to consider quota effects: if a request was routed to dedicated because hosted quota hit, that's sensitive. show enum 'quota_routed' but keep the logs internal.
Jess Nguyen: console UX request: we should have a "Routing playback" panel - given a trace_id it replays policy checks and shows timeline (incoming, tier check, model availability, fallback). small demo would help sales.
Alex Chen: rough api: response header X-Redwood-Route-Trace: <trace_id> and X-Redwood-Route-Reason: <short-reason>. trace_id links to a read-only playback endpoint in console with RBAC.
Samir Rao: infra note: we'd need to store decision snapshots for at least 30 days for rollbacks/analyses. storage budget question. :money_with_wings:
infra-bot: scheduled job created to estimate storage growth for routing traces -> job id 2026-03-18-01.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for routing-traces service on staging at 2026-03-19 04:00 UTC.
Kevin Patel: also need sampling rules. we can't store trace for every single request for high-volume customers. propose: 100% for enterprise plan X, 1% default, and increased sampling during rollouts.
Maria Lopez: rollout integration: when rollout flag changes (canary -> 25% -> 50%), automatically increase sampling for affected traffic and annotate playback with rollout id. makes regression triage much faster.
Jess Nguyen: UX question: should the playback show policy source (console policy vs inherited global)? i'd like a visual cue for 'policy origin' and a highlighted field that says "fallback reason" in red when applicable.
Alex Chen: internal API debate: put routing headers on responses vs responses+events. If we only include on response, async consumers miss it. if we emit an event to syslog/trace pipeline it's consistent but means more plumbing. Thoughts?
Samir Rao: prefer both: lightweight header for immediate downstream, and a routed-decision event to our telemetry pipeline (with trace_id). events get PII redaction and retention rules.
Maria Lopez: redaction rules: remove any user prompt content from decision snapshots. store only metadata: model_id, quantization, region, policy_eval_order, quotas, error_codes. We must document exactly which fields are persisted.
Kevin Patel: also need a mechanism to expire traces on customer's request (GDPR/sensitive). add an API to request deletion by trace_id and a background job to scrub associated artifacts.
Jess Nguyen: will mock up a console card layout: header with trace_id, summary line (routed-> model_a -> fallback->quant4), timeline, policy details collapsed by default, and a "share" button that redacts PII for support.
Alex Chen: timeline event example (for playback):
```
[00:00:000] received req (region=eu-west, customer=tier:standard)
[00:00:002] evaluate policy: prefer-hosted-by-latency
[00:00:010] capacity check failed (hosted eu-west: 92% util) -> mark fallback_candidate
[00:00:011] policy decide -> route to dedicated-quant4 (fallback)
[00:00:012] response sent (X-Redwood-Route-Reason: fallback_capacity; X-Redwood-Route-Trace: rtrace_1769994123)
```
Samir Rao: minor: prefer header name X-RW-Route-Trace to keep header length small. also consider a signed token for trace_id to prevent spoofing.
Maria Lopez: signed token sounds good. include internal-only verification key. console will accept token and show the playback only if RBAC allows.
Kevin Patel: API change risk assessment: this new header is additive and safe. events and storage are bigger work. propose spike for storage + sampling this sprint.
Alex Chen: proposed action items: 1) spike sampling/storage cost (Samir), 2) proto UI mockups (Jess), 3) redact schema + retention policy (Maria), 4) API header naming + token scheme (Kevin). I'll open a tracking ticket and link PRs.
Jess Nguyen: i'll drop a Figma link in the ticket later today.
Samir Rao: taking spike. ETA EOD Friday.
Alex Chen: thanks all — should help observability for routing decisions and make fallbacks less mysterious to customers. :thumbsup:
